stem: Luis has to choose one person at random from four people, $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$. He throws a fair six-sided die. If the score is 1, he will choose $A$. If the score is 2 he will choose $B$. If the score is 3, he will choose $C$. If the score is 4 or more he will choose $D$.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain why the choice made by this method is not random.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Describe how Luis could use a single throw of the die to make a random choice.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: On another day, Luis has to choose two people at random from the same four people, $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$.
parts.text: List the possible choices of two people and hence describe how Luis could use a single throw of the die to make this random choice.
